scalesUsed.notes: G - A - Bb - C - D - Eb - F - G
scalesUsed.application: Foundation for the iconic riff and chord progressions throughout the song
Solo sections and lead guitar fills, especially the extended solo

mainProgression.description: The iconic riff built on parallel fourths moving through the natural minor scale, creating the most recognizable guitar riff in rock history

sectionProgressions.progression: G5 - Bb5 - C5 | G5 - Bb5 - Db5 - C5
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - III - IV | i - III - bV - IV
sectionProgressions.description: Two-bar riff using parallel fourth intervals, with the chromatic Db5 passing chord adding tension in the second bar
Simpler movement between tonic and subtonic, providing space for vocals
More expansive harmonic movement with the IV chord adding brightness before resolving to the tonic

harmonicFunction: G5 (i) - Tonic power chord establishing the dark minor tonality
Bb5 (III) - Major mediant providing modal brightness within minor key
C5 (IV) - Subdominant creating upward harmonic motion and tension
Db5 (bV) - Chromatic passing chord adding dissonance and forward motion
F5 (VII) - Subtonic chord reinforcing the natural minor sound

techniques.name: Parallel Fourth Intervals
techniques.description: The signature technique of the main riff, playing two notes a perfect fourth apart simultaneously on adjacent strings, creating a thick, powerful sound without a full chord

notes: G5 interval: 3rd fret D string + 3rd fret G string (G and C notes)
Bb5 interval: 6th fret D string + 6th fret G string (Bb and Eb notes)
C5 interval: 8th fret D string + 8th fret G string (C and F notes)
Db5 interval: 9th fret D string + 9th fret G string (Db and Gb notes)
All shapes use the same two-string fingering moved up the neck
Use index finger barred across both strings at each fret position
sequence: Place your finger at the correct fret position
Strike both strings simultaneously with a downstroke
Slide to the next chord position
Move through the chord positions in sequence
Return to the starting position to complete the phrase
tips: Keep your fretting hand relaxed - you only need two strings
Mute surrounding strings with light finger contact to avoid noise
Practice the sliding motion between fret positions slowly at first
Focus on even volume between both strings in each interval
Let the notes ring slightly before moving to the next position
details.progression: G5 - Bb5 - C5 | G5 - Bb5 - Db5 - C5 (Main Riff)

techniques.name: Power Chord Rhythm
techniques.description: Standard power chord shapes used in the verse and chorus sections, providing the harmonic foundation beneath the vocals

notes: G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (3rd fret low E, 5th fret A and D strings)
Bb5: 6-8-8-X-X-X (6th fret low E, 8th fret A and D strings)
C5: 8-10-10-X-X-X (8th fret low E, 10th fret A and D strings)
F5: 1-3-3-X-X-X (1st fret low E, 3rd fret A and D strings)
Use root-fifth-octave voicing for fuller sound
Consistent downstroke picking for driving rhythm
sequence: Position fretting hand in standard power chord shape
Play rhythm pattern with steady downstrokes
tips: Keep your wrist loose for relaxed downstrokes
Mute unused high strings by lightly resting fingers across them
Practice shifting between G5 and F5 positions until smooth
Use the full power chord shape for verse sections, intervals for the riff

techniques.name: Minor Pentatonic Solo Phrases
techniques.description: Ritchie Blackmore's solo uses G minor pentatonic with expressive bends and vibrato, showcasing a blues-rock solo approach over a minor key

notes: Based primarily on G minor pentatonic at the 3rd and 15th fret positions
Uses whole-step and half-step bends for expression
Incorporates fast pull-offs and hammer-ons
Vibrato applied to sustained bent notes for vocal-like quality
sequence: Begin in 3rd position G minor pentatonic
Use bending on the B and high E strings for melodic phrases
Transition to 15th position for higher register climax
Resolve phrases back to G root note
tips: Start by learning the G minor pentatonic box shapes
Practice bending in tune before attempting the solo
Focus on Blackmore's phrasing and note choices over speed
Use the backing track to practice timing and feel
details.progression: Over G5 - Bb5 - C5 chord changes

sections.name: Main Riff (Intro)
sections.description: The most iconic guitar riff ever written, using parallel fourth intervals on the D and G strings to create a massive, memorable melody
sections.progression: G5 - Bb5 - C5 | G5 - Bb5 - Db5 - C5
notes: Play on the D and G strings (4th and 3rd strings)
Each interval is a quarter note with slight separation
Second bar adds the chromatic Db5 passing tone before resolving to C5
Let notes ring briefly but with controlled sustain

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse section drops to simpler power chord movement, creating space for the vocal melody while maintaining the dark minor tonality
notes: Switch from fourth intervals to full power chords
Simpler harmonic movement leaves room for vocals
Maintain driving downstroke rhythm throughout
The VII-i movement creates a strong rock cadence

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus expands the harmonic palette with more chord changes, building energy and intensity before returning to the main riff
notes: More chord changes than verse section
C5 to G5 movement creates a plagal (IV-i) feel
Bb5 adds color before final resolution to G5
Builds intensity heading back into the riff

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Ritchie Blackmore's extended solo showcasing blues-rock phrasing with expressive bending, vibrato, and position shifts across the G minor pentatonic scale
notes: Solo is based on G minor pentatonic scale
Uses expressive whole-step bends on the B and high E strings
Combines fast legato runs with sustained bent notes
One of the most celebrated guitar solos in rock history

guitar.pickup: Neck pickup for the warm, thick riff tone; bridge pickup for solo brightness

alternatives: Fender Hot Rod Deluxe with overdrive pedal

settings.middle: 7 (strong mids for the riff to cut through)

effects.distortion: None originally - natural amp overdrive from Marshall cranked up
effects.reverb: Light natural room reverb from amp
effects.other: No effects pedals - Blackmore used guitar volume knob for dynamics

beginner.focus: Learn the main riff using parallel fourth intervals on two strings
steps: Memorize the fret positions: 3, 6, 8, and 9 on the D and G strings
Practice the two-bar riff pattern slowly without a metronome
Work on clean interval shapes with both notes ringing evenly
Build up to 112 BPM tempo gradually with a metronome

intermediate.focus: Add verse and chorus power chord sections with proper rhythm
steps: Learn the full power chord shapes for G5, Bb5, C5, and F5
Practice transitioning between the riff and verse sections
Work on the chorus chord progression with correct timing
Play along with the full track maintaining consistent rhythm
intermediate.timeEstimate: 2-4 weeks for complete rhythm guitar part

advanced.focus: Learn the guitar solo and perfect the overall tone and dynamics
steps: Master G minor pentatonic scale in multiple positions
Learn the solo phrase by phrase with attention to bending accuracy
Work on vibrato technique for sustained notes
Combine all sections into a complete performance with dynamic control
advanced.timeEstimate: 4-8 weeks for complete mastery including solo

commonMistakes: Playing the riff with full power chords instead of two-note fourth intervals
Not muting the surrounding strings, causing unwanted noise
Rushing the rhythm - each note needs its full rhythmic value
Uneven volume between the two strings in each interval
Sliding too quickly between positions without letting notes ring
practiceRoutine: Warm up with chromatic exercises on the D and G strings for 5 minutes
Practice the main riff slowly at 60 BPM, focusing on clean intervals
Increase tempo by 10 BPM increments until reaching 112 BPM
Work on verse power chord transitions for 10 minutes
Play through entire song structure with backing track
focusAreas: Clean two-note interval technique on adjacent strings
Accurate fret position changes along the neck
Consistent rhythm and timing at 112 BPM
String muting to keep unused strings silent
Smooth transitions between riff and chord sections
metronomeWork: Start at 60 BPM playing the riff with quarter notes
Gradually increase to 80 BPM once clean at lower tempo
Practice verse chord changes with metronome at half tempo first
